entities.name: Basilique du Sacré-Coeur de Nancy
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Nancy (Basilique du Sacré-Cœur de Nancy), a neogothic basilica constructed in Nancy, Lorraine, France between 1901 and 1953, is one of the significant Catholic churches of Nancy — a city that already possessed the extraordinary UNESCO-listed Place Stanislas and its 18th-century Baroque heritage — representing the 19th-20th century Sacred Heart devotion movement that produced major basilicas throughout France (most famously the Sacré-Cœur of Paris, 1875-1914) as expressions of Catholic piety in the context of post-1870 French religious-political polarization.

The Sacred Heart devotion (Sacré-Cœur), rooted in the visions of Saint Margaret Mary Alacoque in 17th-century France and institutionalized through the Jesuits, experienced an extraordinary revival after France's 1870 defeat in the Franco-Prussian War and the Paris Commune. Many French Catholics interpreted these disasters as divine punishment for France's secularization and atheism, and the building of Sacred Heart basilicas was conceived as a national act of reparation and consecration. The Paris Sacré-Cœur on Montmartre was the most famous expression; provincial basilicas like Nancy's participated in the same religious-political movement.

Nancy's Basilica of the Sacred Heart, though less architecturally famous than Paris's, is significant in the context of Lorraine — the French-German borderland that was ceded to Germany after 1870 (Lorraine was partially annexed) and remained a contested territory until 1918. The Sacred Heart basilica in Nancy, the regional capital of the unannexed portion of Lorraine, carried particular patriotic and religious meaning for Lorrainers who regarded themselves as guardians of French Catholic tradition.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Nancy — participating in the post-1870 French Catholic national reparation movement, serving as Lorraine's patriotic Catholic monument during the contested French-German border period, and adding neogothic heritage to Nancy's extraordinary Baroque city — is historically meaningful in its regional religious and political context.
